title: GaussTrap: Stealthy Backdoor Attacks on 3D Gaussian Splatting for Targeted Scene Misperception

problem.claim: Backdoor threats in 3D Gaussian Splatting pipelines can cause targeted scene misperception while remaining difficult to detect.

gap.claim: The security vulnerabilities of 3D Gaussian Splatting remain largely unexplored.

contributions.claim: The adaptive density control mechanism of 3DGS enables localized Gaussian proliferation that can embed malicious backdoors into scene geometry while remaining invisible from other viewpoints.
GaussTrap is a three-stage stealthy poisoning framework for 3DGS comprising adversarial injection, geometric stabilization, and global fidelity restoration.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present GaussTrap as a novel stealthy poisoning framework tailored for 3DGS.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks reportedly show reliable targeted visual corruption under trigger conditions while maintaining high rendering fidelity elsewhere.
The reported attack achieves high efficacy with low detectability while preserving photorealism in benign views.

narrative_sequence.summary: 3DGS is used for real-time scene representation and novel view synthesis in safety-critical applications.
Security vulnerabilities in 3DGS have received limited study.
The study identifies a vulnerability in adaptive density control that supports localized malicious geometry changes.
GaussTrap uses staged poisoning to insert imperceptible adversarial Gaussian components.
The authors report targeted corruption under triggers with preserved fidelity in other views and settings.

source_observation.claim: An adaptive mechanism intended to improve detailed reconstruction can also enable localized malicious geometry proliferation.

interpretation.claim: Optimization or reconstruction mechanisms may introduce security risks when their adaptive behavior is not threat-modeled.

application.claim: Security assessments for adaptive 3D rendering pipelines should examine whether control mechanisms can be manipulated to create localized, viewpoint-dependent artifacts.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this lesson generalizes beyond the studied 3DGS setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the trigger conditions or attack metrics.
The abstract does not identify the benchmark datasets or experimental comparisons.
The abstract does not describe defenses, attack assumptions, or limitations.
